text:
Maya L: Quick summary — ran a focused extrapolation bakeoff: SmoothQuant + activation-aware mix (FP8/INT8/GPTQ variants) on redwood-13b with 128k sequence eval set. Dropped raw numbers and a few odd failure cases below.
Sam K: Nice, TL;DR?
Maya L: TL;DR: SQ+activation-aware FP8-mix gives lowest ppl delta (~+1.1%) vs fp16 but has a handful of catastrophic divergence prompts at >100k context; AWQ-int8 variant is cheaper but ppl +3% and more brittle on long numeric sequences. Latency p50 up ~12ms, p99 up ~70-90ms depending on kv-cache touches.
Devon R: Can you paste the exact command and the top-line table?
Maya L: Sure — command used:```python
python tools/run_bench.py \
  --model redwood-13b \
  --quant mix-sq-fp8-int8 \
  --act-aware true \
  --seq 128000 \
  --batch 1 \
  --batches 400 \
  --seed 42
```
Maya L: Top-line (median across 4 seeds, 95% conf):
```
variant                ppl_delta   latency_p50   latency_p99   cost_rel
fp16 (baseline)        0.0%        120ms         450ms         1.00x
SQ+FP8-mix             +1.1%       132ms         520ms         0.62x
AWQ-INT8               +3.2%       128ms         510ms         0.48x
GPTQ-static            +2.8%       125ms         495ms         0.55x
```
Lucas P: Those p99 jumps look scary. Any idea where they come from? kv cache evictions?
Maya L: Most p99s correlate with sequences that cause repeated KV-cache writes across many layers (we saw spike in mem-copy counts). Also activation scale overflow in two specific FFN layers around layer 22/23 for some numeric-heavy prompts.
Sam K: Did you log layerwise act stats? Any outlier ratios?
Maya L: Yep. Quick excerpt: `act_outlier_ratio[layer22] = 2.4%`, `layer23 = 1.9%` for the failing prompts, vs background <0.01% on random shorter contexts. Seems like extrapolation amplifies outliers.
Devon R: Interesting. Suggestion: try per-channel clipping and a tiny bias-correction on act scales. Also test mixing FP8 for those 2 bad layers only.
Maya L: Agreed. I ran a quick ablation: forcing FP16 on layers 22-24 + SQ elsewhere reduced catastrophic failures to zero on the failing set and ppl_delta ~+1.25% (still cheaper than full fp16).
Sam K: Nice hack. How reproducible? Any stochasticity?
Maya L: Repro is decent — same failing prompts trigger divergence ~80% across seeds for AWQ/int8 but only ~5% for SQ+FP8-mix after layer-fixing.
Lucas P: What about accuracy metrics beyond ppl? Any BLEU/QA regressions?
Maya L: We ran a small QA subset (math word problems stretched across context): exact-match drop for AWQ ~6pts, SQ+FP8-mix ~2pts, SQ+layer-fix ~1pt. So SQ mix preserves QA better.
Devon R: Ops note: p99 latency regression might bite SLOs. Can we add a routing policy to prefer fp16 for enterprise customers above x tokens?
Maya L: Good call. We can implement model-variant routing by token count: if seq > 100k route to SQ+layer-fix (or full fp16) depending on tier. Need perf/price tradeoff doc.
ci-bot: Build succeeded: quant-expt/2387654321 (artifacts uploaded) :white_check_mark:
Sam K: Next steps?
Maya L: Action items — 1) Devon to run per-channel clip + small bias correction script across full 128k holdout (due Thu) 2) Lucas to test routing rule simulation for e2e latency/SLO impact (due Fri) 3) I'll prepare short doc with recommended quant profile (SQ default, FP16 fallback for top layers or high-token routes) and cost model.
Devon R: I'll also try a hybrid calibration set (mix of short & extrap prompts) to see if calibration reduces outliers.
Lucas P: I'll mock the routing in the console so we can A/B on a subset.
Maya L: Thanks — filing results under the bakeoff folder. Tagging folks: @Devon R @Lucas P :rocket:
Sam K: Awesome. If we can keep ppl delta <+1.5% with zero catastrophic failures and ~0.6x cost, that's a win.
Maya L: Yup. I'll upload the raw logs and per-layer histograms to the shared bucket and link in the bakeoff doc when ready. :clipboard:
Devon R: small note — saw one prompt where GPTQ static did better on a long regex generation task (odd), adding it to weird-cases list.
Maya L: Noted. We'll add weird-cases appendix. Thanks all.
